profile.entities: Self only. Named externally: IAF, Indian Army, DRDO, HAL, BrahMos (seeker), IMD (radar order); programs LCA Tejas Mk1A, LCA Mk2, AMCA; peer Astra Microwave (mgmt declined to comment); foreign defence OEMs / Germany (EW competitor)

deepdive.sec: Defence electronics — radar/avionics/EW systems (in-house design, IP-driven)

bull_bear.body: Debt-free, net-cash; no leverage taken. Cash deployed into R&D (expensed), capacity expansion and new-product development. No buyback/dividend commentary this call. Focus on improving working-capital cycle.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- Order timing entirely dependent on government/agency approval cycles (HAL, DRDO, MoD) — lumpy, unpredictable.
- Revenue back-ending / quarterly volatility (Q4 −13% YoY despite strong FY).
- Long working-capital cycle (365 days).
- Margin variability from strategic low-margin contracts.
- Execution/air-trial timelines for EW & new radars (1.5–2 yrs); BrahMos seeker production timing (mgmt downplays risk).
- DRDO gating of missile/seeker programs; capex stranded if contracts slip.
- Competition from foreign OEMs and domestic peers (e.g., Astra Microwave moving into systems).
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: Highly bullish and expansive — MD explicitly gave a "first time all-rounded view" on market, investment and scaling, repeatedly stressing growth "substantially higher than guidance" and a multi-thousand-crore ambition. Defensive/irritable on analyst mischaracterisations (denied any "delays" or "poor execution"; insisted execution is fast and good, delays are government-side). Conservative on giving hard timelines/revenue for unproven programs.
bull_bear.title: Mgmt tone

bull_bear.body:
- "Virupaksha" radar (Super Sukhoi) is a DRDO project, NOT a Data Patterns product — mgmt corrected analyst; DPIL has its own equivalent it expects IAF to adopt later.
- Q4 high margin is a mix artifact (no bought-out), not a new run-rate.
- INR1,900cr repeat pipeline is OUTSIDE the INR2,062cr order book and OUTSIDE guidance — large optionality.
- EW self-protection jammer pods already received by IAF, poised for flight testing → medium-term revenue.
- Pursuing electro-optic seekers via an industry partner; wants to become an "electro-optics" not just electronics company.
- Services billed only as performed → does not inflate receivables despite rising services mix.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious

bull_bear.body:
- Strong reputation for delivering high-quality products and services in Defence and aerospace sectors
- Robust domain capability in Radars, Electronic Warfare, Communication systems, Avionics & Satellite Systems
- Significant, sustained investment in R&D allowing continuous innovation ahead of market trends
- Strong internal quality process and quality team
- Scalable business model with potential to build complete systems
- Deep technical expertise in electronic systems design, embedded software development and manufacturing
- Senior personnel associated with the Company for more than two decades, indicating institutional continuity
- Philosophy of investing ahead of opportunities, so products are already developed and validated before programmes are launched by customers
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Heavy dependence on government/PSU customers and Defence spending — Business heavily relies on government contracts, making it vulnerable to fluctuations in government spending and regulatory changes; majority of customers are Government or Public Sector Undertakings.
- Single business segment concentration — Company operates only in one segment — manufacture, sale and service of Defence electronics — with no reportable segment diversification, concentrating all revenue in one industry cycle.
- Long development cycles and high upfront costs straining working capital — The Defence industry involves high upfront costs and long development cycles which can strain financial resources and affect profitability; extensive gestation of development contracts may lead to strain on working capital, and working capital cycles were flagged as challenging.
- Technology obsolescence — Rapid advancements in technology could potentially render existing products and solutions obsolete if not continuously innovated upon, requiring sustained R&D investment to stay current.
- Regulatory, export-control and compliance risk — Changes in government regulations, export controls, or compliance requirements could impact the Company's ability to operate and export its products.
- Supply-chain dependence on external suppliers amid geopolitical instability — Dependence on suppliers for critical components and materials exposes the Company to risks of raw-material shortages, transportation issues, or geopolitical instability, highlighted in the context of the Russia-Ukraine conflict and West Asia crisis; Company noted some delays in sourcing material from global sources though no outright supply failure, and continues evaluating mitigation.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Data Patterns (India) Limited designs, develops, manufactures and services electronic products for Defence and Aerospace customers, spanning Radar and Fire Control Systems, Avionics and Electronic Warfare, Automatic Test Equipment, and repair/overhaul/job-work services. It operates as a single reportable segment, serving predominantly Government and Public Sector Undertaking customers in India along with a small but growing export book.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Radar and Fire Control Systems:** Radars, Fire control systems, Transportable Precision Approach Radar (TPAR), Airborne surveillance radars, Maritime radar applications, Drone detection / counter-drone systems
- **Avionics and Electronic Warfare:** Electronic Warfare suites, Self-protection jammer pods, Avionics systems, Electronic support systems, Advanced surveillance solutions
- **Communication Systems:** Communication equipment
- **Satellite Systems:** Satellite systems (under development)
- **Automatic Test Equipment:** Automatic Test Equipment
- **Service and others:** Repairs, overhaul and job work

latest_quarter.body: FY26 EBITDA 40% (gross 63%). Q4 spike (EBITDA 56%, gross 73%) driven by 100% in-house full-system deliveries with zero bought-out content; weaker quarters reflect strategic low-margin contracts taken deliberately to build full-system/PMO/mechanical capability. Mgmt warns against contract-by-contract margin extrapolation; structural guide is 38–40%.
latest_quarter.title: Margins

latest_quarter.body:
First tracked file for DATAPATTNS (no prior summary in repo). Key Q4 FY26 / FY26 markers vs prior commentary referenced on call:
- Order inflow FY26 ~INR1,121cr, +216% YoY — step-change vs FY25.
- Negotiated-order bucket grew from ~INR1,000cr (prior call) to ~INR1,090cr; some converted; total order book now ~INR2,062cr.
- Q4 revenue −13% YoY but +99% QoQ; FY26 less back-ended (37% in Q4 vs 55% in FY25).
- Cash conversion cycle improved to 365 days (from 428); now targeting 320–340.
- New disclosures: ~INR1,900cr single-vendor repeat pipeline; EW jammer pods accepted by IAF and heading to flight test; AMCA RFP "any time now"; anti-drone product suite entering demos; nine-floor factory expansion underway.
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log

outlook.body:
- Revenue growth ~20–25% over short term; mgmt believes actual will be "substantially higher" if repeat/export orders land early.
- EBITDA margin 38–40%; remain net cash / debt-free.
- Cash conversion cycle targeted to settle at ~320–340 days (from 365).
- Aspiration: build order book of ≥3 years' revenue for predictable growth; scale to multi-thousand-crore over 2–3 years.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body:
- FY26 inflows ~INR1,121cr (+216% YoY), diversified across radar, avionics, EW, services, strategic electronics.
- Order book at Mar-2026 ~INR926cr; incl. negotiated/expected ~INR2,062cr.
- Negotiated bucket now ~INR1,090cr (multiple cases, some already converted), expected to be contracted in next 1–2 months; ~INR100cr of it is services, rest products → product order book heading to ~INR1,500cr+.
- Additional ~INR1,900cr of single-vendor repeat orders on already-delivered products expected to fructify within FY27 (timing not in company's control — govt customers).
- Export order book ~INR53cr (UK repeat business; precision approach radar exported to a European country with site acceptance).
- Services ~38% of current order book / ~INR350cr (AMC, multi-year; billed as performed, so no receivable build-up).
- Largest Q4 order: IMD radar development + service order (~18-month execution).
outlook.title: Order book

outlook.body: Drivers: indigenisation/import substitution, geopolitical defence-capex supercycle (domestic + Europe/UK/US/Japan/Korea exports), repeat orders on accepted products, new product repurposing (anti-drone detection/spoofing/jamming — quick, low-hanging), and seekers/airborne radar/EW programs. AMCA RFP expected "any time now."
outlook.title: Growth

outlook.body:
- Invest ahead of opportunities — develop and validate products before customer programmes emerge, so the Company can participate meaningfully when defence modernisation opportunities open up
- Continuously identify technology gaps and build indigenous solutions in areas where domestic alternatives are limited or unavailable, across radar systems, electronic warfare, communication systems, airborne platforms and strategic defence technologies
- Expand addressable market through innovation, engineering excellence and in-house intellectual property creation rather than only participating in existing markets
- Grow exports as a long-term strategic pillar, building on repeat UK business and expanding engagement across Europe and other international markets
- Pushed 'Process Excellence' to the forefront — streamlining operations and reinforcing governance across all levels to enable responsible scale-up of infrastructure and capability
- Elevate workforce capability through targeted upskilling and enhanced resource utilisation to support a leaner, more agile, high-performance organisation
- Integrate ESG principles across expanding operations, from manufacturing eco-efficiency to community-focused CSR initiatives
- Company operates a debt-free balance sheet and maintains an adequate cash balance to meet strategic objectives; it follows a formal Dividend Distribution Policy (available on the Company website) and has paid final dividends each year (Rs 7.90/share for FY25, Rs 10/share recommended for FY26), with no transfer to General Reserve made in FY26 as retained earnings are used to fund growth. Non-executive director remuneration is governed by criteria including Company performance, independence, contribution to Board discussions and participation in strategic decision-making, limited to sitting fees and profit-linked commission. The Company has no subsidiaries and does not prepare consolidated financial statements.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY26 was described by management as a year of 'historic, tangible expansions' in capability and infrastructure, following a year of vision-setting. The Company continued to build out its Siruseri, Chennai campus, including an EMI-EMC Testing Facility funded from QIP proceeds (against an object of Rs 15.23 Cr, Rs 13.63 Cr had been utilised and Rs 1.60 Cr remained unutilised as at March 31, 2026). QIP proceeds earmarked for product development (Rs 167.24 Cr object) had Rs 131.19 Cr utilised and Rs 36.05 Cr unutilised as at the same date, continuing investment in Radar, Electronic Warfare, Communication and Satellite product lines. Management also referenced 'upcoming infrastructure expansion' built on strengthened internal processes and governance to support the Company's next phase of growth, though no additional named site or capacity project beyond the EMI-EMC facility was disclosed in the routed text.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Rising defence spending, increasing indigenisation, growing demand for advanced electronics and expanding global opportunities cited as key growth drivers going forward
- Growing participation of private industry and increasing government defence allocations under Aatmanirbhar Bharat create what management calls a 'once-in-a-generation opportunity' for Indian defence technology companies
- Order inflow growth attributed to diversified wins across multiple defence and aerospace programmes, reflecting growing customer confidence in the Company's technological capabilities and execution track record
- Growing acceptance of the Company's capabilities in international markets, with increasing interest from customers outside India as global defence spending and armed-forces modernisation rise
- Multiple in-house R&D programmes (electronic warfare suites incl. self-protection jammer pods, airborne surveillance radars, maritime applications, drone detection/counter-drone technologies, electronic support systems) have reached advanced stages of development and validation, positioned as the next phase of growth
- All-time high order book in the Company's history as of FY26 year-end
- Order inflows of approximately Rs 1,121 crore recorded during FY26, representing growth of 216% year-on-year, diversified across multiple defence and aerospace programmes
- Export order book of approximately Rs 53 crore as on date, with continued repeat business from the United Kingdom and active engagement with customers across Europe and other international markets
- Successful development, export and acceptance of the Transportable Precision Approach Radar (TPAR) by a European customer marked as an important export milestone

deepdive.thesis: IP-led, debt-free indigenous defence-electronics house at the start of a multi-year scale-up: order inflows tripled in FY26 (+216% to ~INR1,121cr), order book ~INR2,062cr (incl. negotiated), plus a ~INR1,900cr pipeline of single-vendor repeat orders on already-delivered/accepted products that mgmt expects to convert over the next 12 months. Near-term guidance is a deliberately conservative 20–25% revenue CAGR at 38–40% EBITDA margins, net-cash, but mgmt repeatedly signalled it is targeting a "multi-thousand-crore" company and growth "substantially higher than guidance."

open.item: Product development expenses expected to run at about 20% to 25% of overall revenue in FY24 and continuing in the next few years.
Management flagged delays in customer acceptance and offtake (including HAL delays for Tejas avionics), causing order-intake and delivery timing to slip toward H2FY25.
Management expects the Ashwini LLTR radar requirement to flow down from BEL and convert into a contract in the next 3 to 6 months (couple of quarters), pending finalisation of updated definitions.
One of the two large space radar contracts had its hardware delivered; the second radar is expected to be delivered in the next 6 months, after which the high inventory should come down.
Management expects more than 70% to 80% of the existing on-hand order book to be executed in FY26, plus some portion of orders received during the year.

About INR1,000 crores of negotiated orders (~INR100 crores services, rest products) are expected to convert to contracts in the next 1-2 months, taking product order book to ~INR1,500 crores or higher.
Company targets INR20 billion to INR30 billion (INR2,000-3,000 crores) in new orders over the next 18 months from a robust bidding pipeline.

Management expects to start getting contracts from global (European) OEMs in the next 2-4 months, initially development then leading to recurring quarter-to-quarter multi-system deliveries; plans to build a dedicated export team addressing Europe, US, Japan, Korea, UK.
Board recommended a final dividend of Rs 10 per equity share (Rs 55.98 Cr) for FY2025-26, to be paid on or before August 29, 2026, subject to shareholder approval at the ensuing AGM.
Company is targeting another INR2,000 crores to INR3,000 crores of orders over the next 18 to 24 months from a strong bidding pipeline.

The first variant BrahMos development seeker order is under execution (earlier 3-4 month order already delivered by March); production orders are expected in the next 4-5 months, to be delivered before the middle of next year, and are part of the ~INR1,900 crore expected orders (not order-on-hand).
Management targets revenue growth of around 20% to 25% over the short term for FY27, while expecting actuals to be substantially higher than the guidance number.

Additional single-vendor contracts based on already-supplied/developed products worth about INR1,900 crores are expected to fructify during FY27 (all production orders, already quoted, timing uncertain).
Management guides to maintaining healthy EBITDA margins of 38% to 40% and preserving net cash status.
Management aims to build a three-year order book to scale the company, hoping to achieve this over the next two to three years.
Company reiterated targeting INR2,000 crores to INR3,000 crores of orders over the next 18 to 24 months.
Management expects production and service business contribution to grow to 70%-plus of revenue (from ~55%) over the next 2-3 years as products mature and get approvals, with development at 15-20%.

Company has contracts remaining to be executed on capital account (not yet provided for) amounting to Rs 36.55 Cr as at March 31, 2026, up sharply from Rs 6.80 Cr a year earlier, indicating a step-up in near-term capex activity.
Cash conversion cycle improved to 365 days in FY26 (from 428 in FY25); management expects it to settle at about 320 to 340 days going forward.

Investments in EW suites including self-protection jammer pods for Indian fighter aircraft have been well received by IAF and are poised for flight testing, expected to lead to revenue in the medium term; EW self-jammer suite (2-2.5 year initiative) to conclude within about 1 year.

verdicts.item: Management reaffirmed a bottom-line/IP-driven (not top-line) business model and is repositioning newly designed anti-drone products (passive, active and jamming) for potentially large end applications; also exploring civil aviation electronics (1-4 year horizon).
verdicts.note: 'repositioned some of our products to address... drone detection, spoofing and jamming... in advanced stage of development'; IP-driven (not top-line) model reaffirmed; civil aviation still exploratory…

verdicts.item: Management retained the earlier bottom-line guidance (20%) and declined to raise it despite the extra strategic-contract revenue.
verdicts.note: PAT grew 22%, meeting/beating the retained 20% bottom-line guidance.

verdicts.item: Company has developed a jammer pod and complete EW suite for the Super Sukhoi (offered to and under evaluation with Air Force, funded by QIP), and has signed co-development agreements with foreign multinationals to address worldwide radar/EW requirements, intensifying export focus with a dedicated team.
verdicts.note: 'EW suites, including self-protection Jammer Pods... have been well received by IAF, and we are poised to take the next steps for flight testing'; export team being built.

verdicts.item: Company has responded (RFI) as part of a consortium with BEML and Bharat Forge for the AMCA program, positioning its avionics/radar/EW capability; contract award expected possibly within about 6 months to a year.
verdicts.note: 'AMCA program, the RFP is expected any time now'; shortlisted with Bharat Forge, award still pending.

verdicts.item: Management expects to collect most current receivables (of ~INR667 crores) in H2 and aims to maintain working capital days at a similar level for the full year.
verdicts.note: Working capital improved but cash flow from operations remained weak; large-contract collections still in progress.

verdicts.item: Working capital/cash conversion cycle is at ~343-345 days; management expects it to gradually come down to about 270 days and lower as the mix shifts to production contracts (ex-advances ~310-315 days).
verdicts.note: 'expect it to probably settle down at 320 to 340 days'; the 270-day target loosened and pushed out (WC 365 in FY26).

verdicts.item: Company anticipates capex of about INR150 crores over the next two years for building, test facilities and production lines/infrastructure to meet anticipated growth.
verdicts.note: 'already started investing on capex and infrastructure expansion'; 9-floor factory space being built.

verdicts.item: Management expects about INR1,000 crores of order inflow in H2 FY26 (including ~INR552 crores of already-negotiated contracts to be confirmed), targeting crossing ~INR1,500 crores of total order inflow for FY26, mostly product/production and development (not services).
verdicts.note: FY26 inflows INR1,121cr did not cross the ~INR1,500cr target; negotiated orders slipped ('that has been delayed').

verdicts.item: Management expects margins to improve in H2 with a more balanced product mix and confirmed that ex the strategic contract, Q2 EBITDA margin would have been in the guided 35-40% range; full-year EBITDA margin guidance retained.
verdicts.note: Margins recovered strongly post-Q2; full-year EBITDA margin 40%, within guidance. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Management remains committed to delivering 20% to 25% revenue growth over the medium term while maintaining healthy EBITDA margins and a net debt-free balance sheet.
verdicts.note: FY26 grew 31%, exceeding the medium-term 20-25% target; 'target revenue growth of around 20%, 25% over the short term' reaffirmed.

verdicts.item: Management is confident of achieving its earlier FY26 revenue growth guidance (20-25%), with slight upward movement possible given the strategic contract executed.
verdicts.note: 'overall revenue has been as per guidance, slightly better than guidance'; FY26 grew 31%, exceeding 20-25%.

verdicts.item: Company is in active discussions for joint (co-invested) development of high-end UAV-based radars with a foreign company to address both Indian and global markets.
verdicts.note: 'inquiries have started coming from Europe for building such products... next 2, 3 months... contracts from these global OEMs'.
